title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
abstract: arXiv:2609.30184v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: U.S. employment-discrimination complaints describe complex event sequences that are not explicitly captured by lexical or embedding-based representations alone. We present ARGUS, a source-grounded pipeline that combines a 5W1H-inspired schema, legal-domain models, and LLM-based structured generation to construct document-level Event Knowledge Graphs (EKGs) from CourtListener complaints. ARGUS extracts fact-bearing statements, builds chunk-level event graphs with participant, temporal, and causal structure, and merges them into document-level representations. We evaluate graph quality through human and multi-model assessment and test downstream utility on claim classification and legal QA. The graph-structured classifier outperforms raw and linearized baselines on the held-out set, and EKG-only retrieval improves document-scoped QA, while open-retrieval gains remain limited by low first-stage candidate recall. tldr: 本文提出ARGUS流水线，结合5W1H模式、法律领域模型和LLM结构化生成，从美国就业歧视投诉文本中构建文档级事件知识图谱，在诉求分类和法律问答任务上显著优于传统文本表示方法。
en_tdlr: ARGUS is a source-grounded pipeline that constructs document-level Event Knowledge Graphs from U.S. employment-discrimination complaints using a 5W1H-inspired schema, legal-domain models, and LLM-based structured generation, outperforming raw and linearized baselines on claim classification and improving document-scoped legal QA.
